annotations.title: Find current deals for a need

description: Use when someone wants a kind of product within a budget ('noise-cancelling headphones under 200 €') or one precise product. For a need that names no product ('a housewarming gift'), search one concrete product type you would suggest, not the need as said, and say the type is your suggestion. Returns at most five offers seen in the last three days in France or Germany, each with price, merchant link when known, separate relevance, deal-quality and purchase-feasibility signals, and its unknowns; or 'no_offer' with the reason. max_price, ship_to and exclude are hard limits. Offers marked 'lead' are real but unconfirmed: check the merchant page before presenting them as available. Each offer has a merchant_link status: 'resolved' (merchant_url is the product page), 'pending' (being looked up: repeat the same search after retry_after_seconds, once), 'abandoned' with a reason (no lookup is under way: use merchant_search_url) or 'unknown'. merchant_market is the country of the shop and cross_border is true when it differs from ship_to: delivery there is then unverified. delivery gives the shipping cost the listing stated, not a quote for an address. id identifies the same offer across calls. The merchant's live price is never rechecked: purchase_feasibility stays below 1.0 and every limit on it is named in unknowns. 'no_offer' comes with the limits applied and why recent candidates were left out. A 'no_offer' answer may carry 'alternatives': at most two offers of the same product type, inside the same limits. An alternative is not what was asked: say so to the person, with what 'differs' lists (an 'observed' of null means unknown, not identical).
